summary: Iteration 7: full retest of the new Add Router / Refresh / Delete-router functionality plus regression of all previous suites. Backend: 58 tests run (57 pass, 1 fail) across router inventory CRUD, overview merge, validation, read-only RouterOS resources and Telegram notifications. Frontend: 17-step Playwright E2E on the public URL covering modal open/validation/submit/cancel, metric increment, fleet-table insertion, toast auto-dismiss, refresh refetch, managed-vs-demo remove button, test-connection API call, all 6 drawer tabs and all 6 nav views — every one of the requested acceptance criteria PASSED. One CRITICAL backend defect found: the RouterOS client is invoked with an unsupported kwarg so NO live RouterOS read can ever succeed for a managed router.

critical.issue: ros_call() passes socket_timeout=10 to routeros_api.RouterOsApiPool(), but RouterOS-api 0.21.0 signature is (host, username, password, port, plaintext_login, use_ssl, ssl_verify, ssl_verify_hostname, ssl_context) — no socket_timeout. Every call fails instantly with TypeError: "RouterOS read failed: RouterOsApiPool.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'socket_timeout'" -> HTTP 502. No connection is ever attempted, so 'Test connection' and all live drawer tabs (Logs/PPP Profiles/PPP Secrets/System Time) are permanently broken for managed routers. Fix: drop the kwarg and set the timeout via socket.setdefaulttimeout()/pool.socket_timeout attribute instead (a timeout is still required, otherwise a dead host will hang the worker thread).

minor.issue: RouterOS failures are returned as HTTP 502. The k8s/Cloudflare ingress replaces any 502 body with its own HTML error page, so the sanitized `detail` never reaches the browser — the UI literally renders 'The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare...'. Use a non-502 status (e.g. 424/409/200-with-error-field) so err.response.data.detail survives.

create_router() always stores status='pending', so the row.setdefault('status','managed') branch in overview() is dead code, and the frontend Status map has no 'pending' entry -> newly added routers render as red 'Offline'.

ui_bugs.issue: Backend returns status='pending' for a newly onboarded router but Status() only maps online/warning/offline, defaulting to red 'Offline'. A router that was just added and never tested is shown as Offline, which is misleading. Add a 'pending' state (grey/amber 'Pending').

Group dropdown is limited to existing groups (from overview). Backend accepts any group string, so there is no way to onboard a router into a brand-new group from the UI. Consider a free-text/creatable option.

integration_issues.flow: Test connection / live RouterOS tabs on a managed router
integration_issues.issue: Request is correctly fired to /api/routers/{id}/resources/interfaces (fix verified), but the backend 502 (see critical issue) surfaces to the user as the Cloudflare origin-error HTML text inside the toast and the drawer error panel.

issues: 'Deliver alarms' label sits flush against/overlapping its checkbox (no gap) in the .tg-toggle row at 1920px
Long toast text is clipped by the drawer overlay (toast is centered under the header and slides beneath the 400px drawer)

action_items: CRITICAL: remove the invalid socket_timeout kwarg from routeros_api.RouterOsApiPool() in ros_call() and apply a socket timeout the supported way — currently 100% of live RouterOS reads/actions fail
Stop returning 502 for RouterOS failures (ingress swallows the JSON body); use 424/409 or 200+error so the sanitized detail reaches the UI
Add a 'pending' status style so freshly onboarded routers do not render as 'Offline'
Add gap/spacing between the 'Deliver alarms' checkbox and its label in .tg-toggle
critical_code_review_comments: ros_call(): kwargs are not validated against the installed RouterOS-api version — pin the library in requirements.txt and add a unit-level smoke test for the pool constructor signature.
overview(): row.setdefault('status','managed') is unreachable because create_router() always writes status='pending'.

/app/frontend/src/App.js is a single 354-line file with several 400+ char JSX lines (topbar/page-heading/fleet table). Split into components (Sidebar, Topbar, FleetTable, RouterDrawer) for maintainability.
GET /api/routers and /api/monitoring/overview use .to_list(500) with no pagination — will silently truncate at 500 managed routers.
DELETE /api/routers/{id} does not cascade-delete backup_schedules/backup_history/audit_log rows for the removed router, leaving orphaned documents.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 17 requested acceptance checks passed

context_for_next_testing_agent: All Add Router / Refresh / Delete / toast-auto-dismiss acceptance criteria from iteration 7 are verified working end-to-end via the public URL; no need to retest them unless code changes. The only open blocker is the RouterOS socket_timeout kwarg bug — after the fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_router_inventory.py::TestRouterValidation::test_managed_router_resource_read_fails_gracefully which asserts (a) status 502 is NOT used with an HTML-masked body and (b) the detail contains no 'unexpected keyword argument'. Note pytest.ini runs xdist loadscope, so any cross-class shared state is racy — keep each test class self-sufficient. Two previously-passing assertions (len(routers)==4 in test_readonly_resources.py and test_telegram_notifications.py) were relaxed to >=4 because overview now merges managed routers; test_readonly_resources.py::test_create_router_requires_fernet_key now cleans up after itself.
rca_of_the_issue: RouterOS-api 0.21.0's RouterOsApiPool.__init__ accepts no socket_timeout parameter (verified with inspect.signature). server.py:63 passes socket_timeout=10, so a TypeError is raised before any TCP connect; the broad except in read_resource converts it into HTTP 502 'RouterOS read failed: ... unexpected keyword argument socket_timeout'. Reproduce: POST /api/routers with any host, then GET /api/routers/{id}/resources/interfaces -> 502 in ~0.2s (too fast for a real connect attempt). Mitigation: remove the kwarg; set the timeout with socket.setdefaulttimeout() around the call or via the pool's socket_timeout attribute after construction.
